Zhitong Finance APP reports: $Microsoft (MSFT.US)$ The company is seeking to ensure adequate power supply for its data centers without relying on government subsidies or increasing the burden on other electricity consumers. As artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure continues to expand, the substantial energy demands of data centers have become an increasingly prominent issue in U.S. social and political discourse. Noelle Walsh, President of Cloud Operations and Innovation at Microsoft, stated at a conference in Houston: "We do not want other consumers to foot the bill for our growth. We will bear the costs ourselves." Microsoft plans to invest $117 billion this year in computing infrastructure for AI and cloud computing services. As tech giants continue to expand their data center footprint, issues such as tight power supply, high grid construction costs, and rising residential electricity bills are sparking growing controversy. Data center construction has even become one of the key issues in this month's U.S. midterm elections. The election results, which saw Democrats gain control of Congress, reflect increasing political attention on energy costs and the impact of large-scale technology projects on local communities. As a long-term supporter of OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, Microsoft has consistently emphasized that its data center construction adheres to a "community-first" principle. This means that related projects should deliver tangible benefits to local residents, rather than imposing the negative consequences of rising electricity costs and infrastructure expansion on local communities. In this context, Microsoft is collaborating with energy giant $Chevron (CVX.US)$ and investment firm Engine No. 1 to develop a large-scale data center and power infrastructure project in West Texas, named Project Kilby. The project adopts an independent power supply model, involving the construction of dedicated power generation facilities near the data center to supply electricity directly, thereby reducing reliance on the public grid. This approach is expected to help large technology companies meet growing computing demand while minimizing the impact of data center expansion on other electricity users. However, Project Kilby currently faces regulatory hurdles. Previously, Texas Governor Greg Abbott suspended approvals for new data center projects, hindering the progress of this development plan. In the recent gubernatorial election, Abbott lost to Democratic candidate Gina Hinojosa. Notably, Hinojosa indicated during her campaign that she might adopt a stricter stance on approving data center projects. This suggests that, despite the change in state leadership, relevant projects may still face significant policy uncertainty. Nevertheless, Chevron still plans to proceed with the construction of Project Kilby according to the established schedule, aiming for initial operations by 2028 and full commercial operation by 2031. Jeff Gustavson, President of Chevron New Energies, stated that any project failing to generate net benefits for the local community is ultimately destined to struggle. He emphasized that Project Kilby is expected to create jobs in West Texas and provide stable tax revenue for local governments, thereby ensuring that data center construction not only serves the computing power needs of technology companies but also creates long-term economic value for the host communities. As investment in U.S. AI infrastructure continues to expand, how technology companies address power supply issues has become a key factor influencing the successful implementation of data center projects. Microsoft’s commitment to bear its own energy costs and avoid passing additional burdens onto other consumers highlights that large tech companies are attempting to alleviate the energy and regulatory pressures triggered by the AI construction boom by building their own supporting power facilities and strengthening community cooperation. title: Hot Inflation Data Hammers Yields And Sends Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) Sliding As Anthropic Eyes IPO Valuation - Foreign Policy Journal
content: By David Prior | Nov 11, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis A hotter-than-expected inflation report rattled financial markets Tuesday, pushing bond yields sharply higher and triggering a broad selloff across major equities. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 0.30% on the session, as rising yields weighed on investor sentiment and prompted a rotation away from growth-sensitive assets. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) bore some of the steepest losses among large-cap technology names, with shares tumbling 3.18% as the inflation-driven yield spike pressured high-multiple stocks. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) was not spared, declining 1.85% as the market-wide risk-off tone dragged down even the most widely held names in the technology sector. Nike (NYSE: NKE) also came under pressure, dropping 2.81% in a session that proved difficult for consumer-facing companies alongside their technology counterparts. The inflation report served as the central catalyst for the day’s turbulence, reinforcing concerns that the Federal Reserve may face a more complicated path toward any future rate adjustments. Surging yields typically increase the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, making growth stocks particularly vulnerable to the kind of repricing seen across markets on Tuesday. While equity markets absorbed the inflation shock, attention in the private markets turned to Anthropic, which moved forward with pricing its initial public offering range. Anthropic’s IPO pricing represents one of the most closely watched capital markets events in the artificial intelligence sector, given the company’s prominence among frontier AI developers. The contrast between Tuesday’s risk-off equity session and Anthropic’s forward march toward public markets underscored the diverging dynamics between established public stocks and high-growth private companies seeking fresh capital. Investors will be watching closely in the sessions ahead to determine whether the inflation data marks a one-day disruption or signals a more sustained period of yield pressure and equity volatility. title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Falls 2.2% on Claude Sheets Launch (Nov 10) - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - In the latest Microsoft stock news, shares of Microsoft (MSFT) fell 2.20%, or $12.02, to close at $533.16 on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Financial media tied the drop in Microsoft stock to Anthropic's launch of Claude Sheets, an AI spreadsheet tool that Barron's described as an Excel competitor. Regular-session close on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 4:00 p.m. New York time. Stock prices: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Volume and 30-day average volume: Nasdaq.com. 52-week range: Yahoo Finance daily highs and lows since November 11, 2025. Indices: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the same date. 10-year Treasury yield: U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve for the same date. Follow MSFT's latest price on our Microsoft (MSFT) stock price today page. Microsoft opened at $542.98, below the prior close, and traded as high as $544.19 before sliding to a day low of $526.37. It finished $6.80 above that low, in the lower half of the day's range. Volume of 26.9 million shares ran 11.20% above the 24.2 million share average. The decline was steeper than the broader market. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% to 25,065.88, the S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.30% to 52,231.89, leaving Microsoft 1.46 percentage points behind the Nasdaq. The US 10-year Treasury yield rose 10.0 basis points to 4.98% in the same session. Large technology peers were mixed. Nvidia (NVDA) dropped 5.47%, Apple (AAPL) slipped 0.62% and Alphabet (GOOGL) eased 0.27%, while Amazon gained 1.48%. After the session, Microsoft sits 4.65% below its 52-week high and 52.68% above its 52-week low. The main reported cause was new competition for Excel, Microsoft's spreadsheet software. According to Anthropic's announcement on November 10, Claude Sheets lets teams and Claude "build spreadsheets together, collaboratively organize data, create and edit formulas, and work across multiple tabs." As reported by Engadget, files built in Claude Sheets can be exported to Excel, and the tool is in beta for Claude subscribers on web, desktop and mobile. Barron's linked Microsoft's decline to the launch, describing Claude Sheets as an Excel competitor that lets customers build full spreadsheets from simple prompts. The publication also noted that Microsoft has ways to defend itself against the competition. The session also reshuffled the market-value rankings. Per Benzinga, Microsoft briefly overtook Nvidia on Tuesday to become the world's second-most valuable company for the first time since June 2025, as fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair deepened Nvidia's selloff and erased the $1.84 trillion market-value lead Nvidia held on October 6. Benzinga noted that Nvidia regained second place by early afternoon. Benzinga added that Nvidia reports earnings on November 17, leaving the race for second place among the most valuable companies unsettled.
